docs.title: Home
docs.text:
simple-pip

A cross-platform extension that adds a button to pop out videos using the Picture-in-Picture API.

docs.title: Chromium Browsers (i.e. Google Chrome)
docs.text:
1. Download the latest release and unzip it
  2. Open Chrome's extension page (chrome://extensions)
  3. Make sure Developer mode is enabled on the top right
  4. Select Load unpacked
  5. Select the release folder's src directory

docs.title: Mozilla Firefox
docs.text:
1. Download the latest release and unzip it
  2. Open Firefox's debugging page (about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox)
  3. Select Load Temporary Add-on...
  4. Select the manifest.json file inside the release folder's src directory

docs.title: Using the extension
docs.text:
To enter Picture-in-Picture mode, click the extension icon or press Alt+P. It will pop out the largest video on the page you're currently viewing.

To exit Picture-in-Picture mode, click the icon or press Alt+P again. If a video is in picture-in-picture mode, it will return to the page.

docs.title: Using light mode icons
docs.text:
If you use Light Mode, a set of supplementary icons are available under the light-mode-icons branch.

  1. Download the light mode icons branch and unzip it
  2. Make sure you have the latest release downloaded
  3. Before installing the extension, replace the images in src/assets with the ones you downloaded
  4. Now you can install the extension!

docs.title: How to use simple-pip with other desktop apps
docs.text:
You can use this extension with most other apps built using Electron, since they allow you to execute code with the console.

Here's a tutorial I made if you're interested:

  1. Open a stream or video on any Electron app.

  2. Copy the extension's main script to your clipboard.

  3. Open the developer tools on Twitch by pressing Ctrl+Shift+I (Windows) or ⌘+⌥+I (macOS).

  4. Press Console in the top bar.

  5. Paste the code and press enter to execute it.

It's a hacky method, but at least it works until other apps come up with their own official methods.

docs.title: Source code
docs.text: The source code for the extension is available on GitHub.

docs.title: via Releases
docs.text:
1. Download the latest release and unzip it
  2. In Chrome: navigate to chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select the src directory
  3. In Firefox: navigate to about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox, click Load Temporary Add-on..., and select src/manifest.json

docs.title: via main branch
docs.text:
1. Download the GitHub repository's code
  2. Unzip the file
  3. In Chrome: navigate to chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and select the src directory
  4. In Firefox: navigate to about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox, click Load Temporary Add-on..., and select src/manifest.json
